ms.report:
The goals for Milestone 1 were as follows:
・Milestone 1: UX/UI Implementation (1 Month) - The activities listed here took place in the last thirty days. 
・Research Existing Solutions - We evaluated polling applications. We examined JD Powers, as well as several open source simple polling systems.
・Build User Journey/User Experience - We walked through our existing user journey, and identified the appropriate locations to implement the polling system both in the administrative areas, as well as the front end.
・Implement UI in Figma - The UI is implemented in Figma according to the needs of our lead developer.

There was concern from one of the reviewers in the previous round of approvals that they did not see the user journey, and did not understand the changes in the UI. Our designers are suggesting a new UI improvement to our tooling. We added the user journey to the Figma, and we brought back both the old UI and the new UI so that reviewers can see both.
Our deliverable is a publicly available Figma document. That document is located here: https://www.figma.com/file/9ITnw8wdzGQxt7ZPy3Ooik/DripDropz-Open-Source-Voting-Gated-Polling?type=design&node-id=0%3A1&mode=design&t=t44G7XHIMakkmhp9-1

*Note on Wallet Connectivity
The application is deployed across two environments which require the wallet to be set to the correct network.
Mainnet deployment
https://vote.resi.works/
Requires wallet to be set to Mainnet
Pre-prod deployment
https://onchain-vote.duckdns.org
Requires wallet to be set to PreProd
If a wallet is connected to the incorrect network, connection and transaction functionality will not operate correctly.
We have confirmed full functionality using Eternl (verified complete CIP-30 adherence) wallet across both environments. Some wallet providers may have limitations or inconsistencies depending on network configuration. Some wallets may not be completely adhering to CIP-30 and would be outside the scope of this project.

Problem Statement
Cardano lacked an accessible and standardized way to conduct gated polling based on verifiable wallet ownership. While voting mechanisms existed, there was no widely available system that allowed communities to restrict participation based on token or NFT ownership in a flexible and reusable way.
This created a gap in governance tooling where participation could not be easily aligned with stake, membership or asset-based identity. Without gating mechanisms, polls could not reliably reflect the structure or intent of a given community.
Proposed Solution
This project delivered a gated polling system as part of the DripDropz open source voting stack. The system enables communities to create polls with rule-based eligibility using wallet verification and token ownership.
Participation can be restricted based on specific assets, allowing governance models to reflect real membership, stake or role-based access. The system integrates directly with wallet authentication and provides a seamless user experience for both poll creation and participation.
The solution was designed to be modular, reusable and easily deployable without requiring custom development.

The project aligns with the goals of the Products and Integrations challenge by delivering open source infrastructure that enables real world blockchain usage.
